title: Finding what is lost: a tour of ABYSSAL
desc: A guided, screenshot-led tour of ABYSSAL, a local-first Bayesian search workbench for finding lost aircraft, ships and people.

title: A map that refuses to lie
desc: The design of ABYSSAL's map: the context/evidence firewall, perceptually ordered colour, credible regions, honest resolution, sketching evidence on the map, certain area statements and offline audit packs.

title: The arithmetic of not finding
desc: The mathematics of Bayesian search in ABYSSAL: log-space grid updates, negative evidence, the coverage fallacy, contamination likelihoods, repeat credit, KL divergence in bits and minimum-KL area statements.

title: Five echoes, one witness
desc: An essay on correlated evidence and provenance in ABYSSAL: geometric pooling of same-source reports, per-item versus whole-source influence in bits, and why humans must admit evidence.

title: Where next, and when to stop
desc: Optimal search allocation (water-filling), expected value of information, mutual information per pound, the search-to-exhaustion curve and stopping rules in ABYSSAL's Where-next and Plan Studio.

title: Signals from the deep
desc: The physics behind ABYSSAL's Signal Lab: SAR ship detection, Kelvin wakes and the azimuth shift, AIS association and dark vessels, hydroacoustic TDOA localisation, ring detection, calibration, and impact ring waves as a dispersive clock.

title: The operating picture
desc: A tour of ABYSSAL's Ops console: live ADS-B and AIS, dark-vessel and orbiting-aircraft flags, SGP4 satellites, environmental layers, leeway drift, bearings fixes, shadow chronolocation, track-gap reach ellipses, and the multi-target watchlist.

title: Three cases, two refusals
desc: ABYSSAL's three reference cases: the Merchant Royal (1641) and the uncertainty of a seventeenth-century league, MH370's satellite arcs and a particle filter that refused to publish, and a chronological held-out backtest of the AF447 search with its hindsight-bias traps.

title: Building it honestly
desc: The rules that keep ABYSSAL honest: invariants, the engine audit, the calibration gate, the mistakes they were written to prevent, and where calibrated probability over space and time is worth paying for.

title: ABYSSAL — honest probability for finding what is lost
desc: A nine-part series on ABYSSAL, a local-first Bayesian search workbench: guided tours, the mathematics of negative evidence and correlated sources, value of information, physics-screened detectors, live operating pictures, historical backtests, and the rules that keep it honest.

title: Page not found
desc: This page does not exist. Find ABYSSAL, the writing and the real-data results from here.

title: Rory Millard
desc: Rory Millard — MEng Engineering Science, University of Oxford (First Class, ranked 1st of ~180). AI, robotics, aerospace, quantum sensing, and weak-signal detection.

title: Inside ABYSSAL: one contract, sixteen engines
desc: The whole of ABYSSAL in one chart: inputs with receipts, sixteen physics-based signal engines that share one contract, an admission gate, a log-space belief engine and the decisions on top. Plus every engine, with screenshots, maths and calibration.

title: ABYSSAL on real data: seven studies, with receipts
desc: ABYSSAL's engines run on real satellite radar, survey bathymetry, Sentinel-2 imagery and public records, scored against truth they never saw: buoys, ship transponders, nautical charts and a real wreck.

title: MH370 in ABYSSAL: From Zero Data to Full-Physics Fuel & Terrain Fusion v3
desc: A complete progressive raw-data investigation of Malaysia Airlines flight 370 inside ABYSSAL's native workbench: starting from 0 observations (30.7M km²), adding ACARS, Inmarsat BTO/BFO, and CSIRO drift; 3D probability and seabed surfaces; 4,400 autopilot paths; Trent 892 fuel-burn physics; 155,000 non-steady trajectories; 252 IMOS hydrophone transients recovering Curtin's 01:33 UTC events; 3D ETOPO SOFAR ray-blocking; NOAA OISST barnacle SST; and terrain-aware sonar POD.
